full_judgment:
The Rule has been obtained by the plaintiff against the judgment and decree dated 15-11-1990 of the court of Subordinate Judge, Cox's Bazar in Other Appeal No. 148 of 1988 affirming the judgment and decree dated 3-9-1988 of the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar in Other Suit No. 14 of 1988 rejecting the plaint on the ground of res judicata upon an application filed under Order 7 rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. The court of first instance, which was affirmed by the court of appeal below, dismissed the suit on the finding that the same was barred by res judicata in that plaintiff as against the ex parte decree obtained by the defendant No.1, herein opposite party, in 'Other Suit No. 15 of 1985 filed Miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 13 CPC on the allegation of suppression and non-service of summons and being unsuccessful filed appeal which was also without any fruit and that on the self-same allegation has filed the instant suit i.e. Other Suit No. 14 of 1988 previously numbered Other Suit No. 27 of 1987 of the court of Assistant Judge, Teknaf.

3. Plaintiff in the plaint, among others, has averred as follows:

৫) সুচতুর বিবাদী ১৯৮৫ সনে ১৫নং অপর অত্র আদালতে নালিশী জমির তজন্য অধীন বাদীর বিরুদ্ধে তথাকথিত অনুমতি প্রত্যাহার গৃহ উৎপাটনে নালিশী জমি খাস দখল পাওয়ার জন্য মামলা দায়ের করিয়া আদালতের পদতিকের যোগাযোগে কোন সমন বা বিজ্ঞপ্তি এই বাদীর উপর জারী না করিয়া তৎসুমুদয় গোপন করিয়া বিগত ১৫-৭-৮৫ইং তারিখে এক তঞ্চকতামূলক এবং একতরফা ডিক্রী হাসিল ককওে বলিয়া বিগত ১৬-১২-৮৫ ইং তারিখে বিশ্বস্ত সূত্রে উক্ত এক তরফা ডিক্রীর কথা জানিয়া তল্লাশে সম্যক অবগত হইয়া তৎ বিরুদ্ধে দেওয়ানী আইনের কার্য্যধারা মতে ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করা সত্ত্বেও উক্ত ডিক্রী জারীর কথা date of knowledge প্রমান করিতে না পারায় অজুহাতে অধীনের আনীত মামলা খারিজ হওয়ায় তৎবিরুদ্ধে আপীল করিয়াও কোন সুরাহা করিতে অপারগ হইয়া বর্তমানে আকারে অত্র মামলা দায়ের করতঃ উক্ত হুজুর আদালতের অপর ১৫ নং মামলার ১৫-৭-৮৫ ইং তারিখে এক তরফা তঞ্চকতা ডিক্রী এবং উক্ত আদলতের ১৯৮৫ সনের ৩২নং অপর জারী মামলা যোগাযোগ তঞ্চকতা মূলক, ফেরবী ও তৎদ্বারা অত্র বাদী বাধ্য নহে মর্মে প্রতিকার চাহিয়া সুনির্দিষ্ট প্রতিকার আইনের ৪২ নং ধারা মতে অত্র মামলা করিতে বাধ্য হইলেন। উক্ত রায় ও ডিক্রী বাদীর বিরুদ্ধে বলবৎ নহে এবং তৎদ্বারা বাদীর স্বত্ব নষ্ট হয় নাই। বাদী নালিশী জমিতে গৃহ নির্মানে দখলকার আছে। বিবাদী উক্ত ১০/৮৫ নং মামলার ডিক্রী বলে জারী দিয়া দখল লইবার এবং দাবীর গৃহ উৎপাটনের জন্য অগ্রসর হইলে বাদী অপূরনীয় ক্ষতির সম্মুখনি হইবে। তাই অত্র মামলা বিচাপর হওয়ায় সাপেক্ষে বিবাদী যাহাতে নালিশী জমিতে দখল লইতে না পারে তৎজন্য বিবাদীর প্রতি এক অস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞা প্রচার হওয়া আবশ্যক।

৬)  উক্ত কথিত এক তরফা তঞ্চকা এবং তঞ্চকত ডিক্রী মুলে উক্ত অপর জারী মামলা দ্বারা এই বাদী মোটেই বাধ্য নহে। উক্তরূপ কার্য্যদি বিবাদী দুর্লালসা, বে আইনী ও বে ধারা মতে নালিশী জমিটুকু আত্মসাৎ করার কু-উদ্দেশ্যে করিয়াছে। and thereupon sought the relief primarily as follows:

অতএব, প্রার্থনা যে,

(ক) কক্সবাজার মুনসেফী আদালতের ১৯৮৫ সনের অপর ১৫নং মামলার গত ১৫-৭-৮৫ ইং তারিখের একতরফা তঞ্চকী ডিক্রী ও তৎমূলে উক্ত আদালতের ১৯৮৫ সনের অপর জারী৩২ নং মামলার আদেশ রদ ও রহিত ক্রমে তৎদ্বারা বাদী বাধ্য না থাকা, নালিশী জমিতে বাদীর খরিদা স্বত্ব সাব্যবস্থাক্রমে নালিশী জমিতে বাদীর তমাদী স্বত্ব সাব্যেস্তর ডিক্রী দেওয়ার।

(খ) বিবাদী যাহাতে উক্ত মোকদমায় ডিক্রী বলে জারী মোকদ্দমা জারী দিতে না পারে তৎমর্মে এক চিরস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞা দেওয়ার আদেশে দিতে,

(গ) সম্যক আদালত, রায় দেওয়ার অথবা আদালতের ন্যায় বিচারে বাদী অন্য যে ভাবে বিবিধ প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে তাহা পাওয়ার ডিক্রী দিতে আজ্ঞা হয়।”

4. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the courts below erred in law in rejecting the plaint on the ground of res judicata in that facts and matters upon which Other Suit No. 14 of 1988 has been filed being not the same or similar to the facts and matter upon which Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 13 CPC was filed for setting aside the ex parte decree obtained in Other Suit No. 15 of 1985. In elaborating the submission so made learned Advocate submits that in Other Suit No. 14 of 1988 the plaintiff has challenged the legality of the decree itself on the ground that facts averred in the Other Suit No. 15 of 1985 in support of the relief sought was untrue and, as such, the decree so obtained in the said Other Suit No. 15 of 1985 has in no way affected title of the plaintiff and that in assailing the ex parte decree incidentally averred that summons of the suit in which ex parte decree was obtained also suppressed and not served upon the defendant of the said suit. He also submits that the courts below erred in holding that the remedy sought as provided in Order 9 rule 13 CPC against ex parte decree is without success and thereupon if the defendant of the earlier suit as plaintiff filed suit for setting aside the ex parte decree the same is barred by res judicata. In support of the aforesaid submission the learned Advocate referred to the case of Sirish Chandra Jana vs Kalachand Maity reported in AIR 1957 Calcutta) 242 and the case of Iyezuddin Seikh and others vs Abdul Karim Sk. and others reported in 42 DLR 154.

5. The learned Advocate for opposite party No.1 in refuting the contentions of the petitioner submits that plaintiff petitioner having been unsuccessful in setting aside the ex parte decree dated 15-7-1985 passed in Other Suit No.15 of 1985 in the proceeding initiated upon in application under Order 9 rule13 of the Code or Civil Procedure up to appellate stage on the finding that summons of the said other suit was served on the defendant i.e. the plaintiff of the instant suit, being suit No. 14 of 1988 and that having not moved the superior Court as against the order of the appellate Court below the suit filed on the self same averments ie suppression and non service of summons has rightly been held by the courts below barred by res judicata and consequent thereupon has quite legally rejected the plaint as per provision of Order 7 rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

6. On perusal of the material portion of the averments made in the plaint quoted above it is seen that plaintiff has not filed the suit for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 15-7-85 as was passed in Other Suit No. 15 of 1985 merely on the grounds of suppression and non-service of summons but also on the grounds that the averments made in denial of the title of the defendant in seeking the relief in Other Suit No. 15 of 1985 and ultimately obtained the relief ex parte were untrue and, as such, the decree so obtained has not affected right, title and interest of the plaintiff of the instant suit in the land in suit and that as the decree obtained in Other Suit No. 15 of 1985 involved right, title and interest of the plaintiff of the instant suit so he has sought the relief in the suit by way of declaration of his title upon setting aside the ex parte decree.

<u>7. Since the plaintiff has not filed the suit not merely on the ground of suppression and non- service of summons but also upon averring that the facts upon which the decree was obtained in the earlier suit were not true arid that ex parte decree so obtained has included his title and, as such, he has been compelled to file the suit for declaration of his title upon setting aside the ex parte decree. So in the suit filed plaintiff is first to prove his tide and if so succeeds then the further relief for setting aside the ex parte decree would be required. In this connection view expressed on the matter similar to the matter involved in the instant case in a case reported in AIR 1957 (Calcutta) 242 may be referred to and the same is as follows:</u>

<u>"It is settled law that where the fraud alleged is of such kind as to attack the suit itself and not merely the regularity- or sufficiency of the service or the proceedings, a suit by a person on whom no summons was served, for setting aside the ex parte decree is maintainable. It is also settled law that mere falsity of claim and or perjured evidence if non-service of summons be not proved will not support the action. The plaintiff, therefore, in a suit for setting aside an ex parte decree on the ground of fraud when he was unsuccessful in his application for setting aside the ex parte decree on the ground of non service of summons must prove some kind of fraud, which affects the suit itself and not merely the regularity or sufficiency of the service or the proceeding, in addition to non-service of summons in order to obtain decree. Falsity of claim would amount to such fraud, though possibly mere perjured evidence, unless the claim was false, would not. The appellant has contended that the rejection of the present plaintiff’s application for setting aside the ex parte decree under Order 9 rule 13 CPC upon the finding that the summons was duly served in the mortgage suit would operate as res judicata to bar the present suit. We do not think that contention is sound in law. There were no doubt allegations also of perjured evidence and fraudulent suppression of summons. But those were really treated as part of the main allegation of fraud that the claim, that is, the suit itself, was a false one, for which there was absolutely no foundation and on or in which a fraudulent ex parte decree was obtained. The Order 9 rule 13 of Civil Procedure Code proceeding again was decided merely on the finding that non-service of summons was not proved. The finding that summons was served, does not, in our opinion in the context in which it appears, mean anything more. The questions of fraudulent suppression of summons or the falsity of the claim which might well have proved a motive for such suppression was not at all considered. In these circumstances, no question of res judicata arises in the present case. I therefore, reject the appellant's plea in that behalf."</u>

8. In the aforesaid case it has also been held that a suit by a defendant who previously was unsuccessful in the proceedings initiated under Order 9 rule 13 Civil Procedure Code for setting aside the ex parte decree is a suit maintainable if the same is filed attacking the claim in the suit in which ex parte decree was obtained falsely and challenge the suit as a false suit.

<u>9. The plaintiff has filed the Other Suit No. 14 of 1988 challenging the legality of the ex parte decree dated 15-7-1985 obtained in Other Suit No. 15 of 1985 averring that the claim in the suit wherein ex parte decree was obtained was untrue and thereupon the decree obtained in the said Other Suit No. 15 of 1985 clouded the title of the plaintiff in the land. Miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 13 CPC was filed alleging suppression and non-service of summons and the said case was disposed of as regards that. There the question of falsity of claim in the suit was not matter in issue and, as such, did not come up for consideration nor decision was given as to that. The courts below upon the view that averments in Other Suit No. 14 of 1988 and also in the miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the legality of the ex parte decree were self same averments and the grounds too and thereupon rejected the plaint on the ground of res judicata. The view so taken being not correct and, as such, committed an error of law in rejecting of the plaint.</u>

<u>In the result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. Judgment and order dated 15-10-1990 passed in Other Appeal No. 148 of 1988 of the court of Subordinate Judge, Cox's Bazar affirming the judgment and decree dated 3.9 1988 of the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar in Other Suit No. 14 of 1988 is set aside. The Other Suit No. 14 of 1988 is restored to its original file and number. Send down the LC Records at once.</u>

End.

lawyer:
Abdus Sobhan Tarafder with Ambia Bulbul Reza, Advocates------For the Petitioners. 
Md Rezaul Huq, Advocate------For the Opposite Party Nos. 2-7 
Deb Das Samadder with Tapash Kumar Biswas, Advocates------For the Opposite Party Nos. 1 & 8.
parties:
Jarina Khatun & others  ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Gani Howlader & others   ------ Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
This Rule was obtained by plaintiff upon making an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against judgment and decree dated 12-6-1995 passed by Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 298 of 1993 affirming those dated 12-9-1993 passed by Assistant Judge at Bakhergonj in Title Suit No. 143 of 1984 dismissing the suit.

2. The plaintiff Tayeb Ali instituted the suit for declaration of his title in the suit land and also for a declaration that the VP case initiated in respect of the suit land is illegal, void and without any lawful authority. On the death of Tayeb Ali, his heirs, present petitioners, after being substituted continued with the proceedings.

3. The plaint case, in short, is that, 8 annas of plot No. 1522 measuring 0.08 acre, and 0.31 acre of plot No. 1524 appertaining to RS Khatian No. 2325 and SA Khatian No. 992 originally belonged to Kashem Ali and Sorju Bala. Other 8 annas of plot No. 1522 was owned and possessed by the plaintiff and SA Khatian Nos. 1446 and 1333 were recorded in his name. The suit land measuring 0.39 acre was purchased by Kali Mohan Mukhopadhya on an auction sale held on 5-1-1953. Said Kali Mohan Mukhopadhya obtained sale certificate and got possession of the land through court on 18-4-1954.

4. While Kali Mohan was thus owner in possession of the said land transferred the same by registered kabala dated 8-6-1962 to Afsar Ali Howlader and Mokter Ali Howlader and delivered possession to them. Thereafter, said Afsar Ali Howlader and Mokter Ali Howlader transferred the suit land by a registered deed dated 10-4-1967 to the original plaintiff. The plaintiff possessed the suit land since then till his death. After the death of the plaintiff, the petitioners are in possession of the suit land.

5. In order to grab the suit property, one Kadam Ali got the VP Case No. 43/80 initiated and on 2-6-1980 obtained lease. When the plaintiff went to pay rents to the Tahsil Office, the Tahsilder declined on 1-12-1981 to receive the rent and therefore, the original plaintiff for the first time came to know that the land was leased out as vested property. Such action of vested property authority cast a doubt over his title.

6. Defendant Nos.1 and 2, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Bakhergonj and Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal were the original defendants and defendants 3, 4, 5 and 6 were subsequently added. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 though filed a written statement but ultimately did not contest the suit. The courts below therefore, did not record their case as stated by them in their written statement in the judgment. Defendant No.3 having died his heirs defendant Nos. 3(Ka) to 3(Chha) and defendant No.4 jointly filed a written statement and contested the suit. Similarly, defendant Nos. 5 and 6 also contested the suit by filing another written statement.

7. The case of the defendant Nos. 3(Ka) to 3 (Chha) and 4, in short, is that, Kashem Ali died unmarried in 1956 and the suit land devolved upon his uncle Saijuddin Howlader. On the death of Saijuddin Howlader defendant No. 3(Ka) and defendant No.4 inherited the said lands. Defendant Nos. 3 and 4 challenged the enlistment of the suit property as a vested property in Title Suit No. 404 of 1983 instituted in the Second Court of Munsif at Barisal and the said Title Suit was re-numbered as 264 of 1984 in the Court of Assistant Judge at Bakhergonj on transfer. The said suit was decreed on contest against the Government and defendant Nos. 5 and 6 declaring VP Case No. 43 of 1980 as illegal and without any lawful authority. They also claimed to be in possession of the suit land on payment of rents. Defendant No.3 transferred some lands to defendant No. 3(Ka) by a deed of gift dated 24-5-1989.

8. Defendant Nos. 5 and 6 filed the written statement denying the case of the plaintiff and also that of defendant Nos.3 and 4. They contended that both Kashem Ali and Saraju Bala migrated to India. Before leaving for India, Kashem Ali sold the suit land along with other land to their father. Thereafter, the heirs of only uncle of Kashem Ali executed and registered a sale deed. They mainly contended that as they were in possession of the suit land the vested property authority granted lease of the suit land to them and they are in possession.

9. On the pleadings, various issues including the issue whether the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and whether the plaintiff has any right, title and interest and possession in the suit land were framed.

10. The trial Court on consideration of the statements of PW 1 Alfaz Ali Howlader, son of late Tayeb Ali Howlader, the original plaintiff, that his father did not possess the suit land by sale deed and that defendant No.3 possessed the suit land, came to a finding that as the plaintiff did not claim to be in possession, the suit for declaration of title simpliciter under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is not maintainable. Accordingly, the trial Court dismissed the suit.

11. On the appeal, the appellate Court also affirmed such findings of the trial Court and dismissed the appeal thereupon.

12. Mr Abdus Sobhan Tarafder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, drew my attention to the fact that in the appeal, the petitioners made an application for amendment of the plaint on the ground that aforesaid PW 1 did not make such a statement that his father did not possess the suit land by virtue of purchase or that defendant No. 3 possessed the suit land. PW 1 actually deposed that they possessed the suit land by virtue of purchase and the defendant No.3 did not possess the suit land. In the first sentence 'No' was added and in the last sentence 'No' was omitted due to mistake. They, therefore, prayed for adding further relief for confirmation of possession in the suit land as consequential to the main prayer for declaration of title on payment of ad-valorem court fee. Without applying its mind the appellate Court rejected the said application as irrelevant and belated. Mr Abdus Sobhan Tarafder also submitted that in the trial Court, the plaintiff proved their title and possession but the trial Court without considering the evidence on record disposed of the suit on those mistaken statements as recorded. Appellate Court also without properly framing the points for determination and discussing the evidence on record disposed of the appeal by a non- speaking judgment in confirming the judgment of the trial Court and the judgment of the appellate Court is no judgment in the eye of law, particularly, under Order 41 rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

13. Mr Rezaul Huq, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, submits that the judgment of the appellate Court being a judgment passed in affirmance of that of the trial Court need not to be so elaborate as that of a reversal. He 'further submits that when PW 1, son of the original plaintiff, Tayab Ali admitted in his evidence that his father did not possess the suit land on the basis of a 'Kabala' and that the defendant No. 3 possessed the suit land, no fruitful purpose would be achieved by remand. He also cited the cases reported in 43 DLR (AD) 125 and 14 BLD (AD) 229.

14. With regard to the prayer for amendment of the plaint, he submits, the application was filed for addition of a prayer for a confirmation of possession and not recovery of possession. On the aforesaid statements of PW 1, the plaintiffs have no chance of success in getting such relief.

I5. Lastly, he submits that if the facts and circumstances of the case necessitate any remand, the case should be sent to the appellate Court and not to the trial Court in view of the delay already occasioned in the proceeding of the suit.

16. I have perused the judgments of the courts below and the revision application upon which the above Rule was issued. I have also examined the evidence, both oral and documentary, on record.

17. The case of the plaintiffs-petitioners is that, Kashem Ali and Sarujo Bala were the original owners in possession of the suit lands. Then, Kali Mohan Mukherjee purchased the suit lands in an auction held on 6-1-1953. He obtained a sale certificate and got physical possession of the lands on 18-4-1954. He also annulled all encumbrances. While Kali Mohan was thus in possession, he transferred the suit lands by a registered deed of sale dated  8-6-1962 to Afsar Ali Howlader and Mokter Ali Howlader. These two brothers, Howladers possessed for some time and then, sold the suit lands to Tayeb Ali, father of the present plaintiffs, by registered sale deed dated 10-4-1967. Tayeb Ali possessed the suit lands for more than the statutory period of 1iyears and then died leaving the present plaintiffs as his only heirs and legal representatives. During the survey under the state acquisitions, the record of rights in respect of the suit lands were wrongly prepared in the names of said original owners, Kashem Ali and Sarujo Bala who were divested of all their interest in the suit lands after the auction sale, and such record had no basis but cast a doubt on the title of the petitioners.

18. On 1-12-1981, the plaintiff for the first time came to know that VP case was started in respect of the suit lands and one Kadam Ali obtained a yearly lease.

19. After due-consideration of RS Khatian Nos. 2325 and 2326, Exhibit 'Cha' and 'Cha-1', the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 295 of 1956, Exhibit No. 3 and revenue sale, Exhibit No. 8, the trial Court found that Kali Mohan Mukherjee purchased the suit lands in auction. Kali Mohan Mukherjee transferred to Afsar Ali Howlader and Moktar Ali Howlader by a registered deed of sale dated 18-6-1962 Exhibit No. 4. Then, Afsar Ali Howlader and Mokter Ali Howlader sold the suit lands to Tayeb Ali by a registered deed of sale dated 10-4-1967, Exhibit No. 4(Ka).

20. The trial Court also found the notice Exhibit No. 2 by which Kali Mohan annulled all the encumbrances and his employees collected rents from the 'Karsha' raiyots. But the court was of the view that the right or interest of the 'Karsha' raiyots was not disappeared. No proceeding was instituted for eviction of the 'Karsha' raiyots. The SA record of rights was prepared in the names of Kashem Ali and Sarujo Bala to the extent of 12 annas and 4 ann as respectively. This finding of the trial Court is however contrary to the case of both defendants 3 and 4 and also of defendants 5 and 6. Their common case is that, during the partition in 1947, both Kashem Ali and Sarujo Bala migrated to India and settled there. Kashem Ali died there. In view of its own findings on title as stated above, the finding of the court that Kali Mohan Mukherjee possessed the suit lands was not proved is not only incongruous but also contrary to the pleadings as well as the evidence on record.

21. The trial Court also found that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 264 of 1984, declared the initiation of a VP Case in respect of the suit lands illegal, and without any lawful jurisdiction, (Exhibit No. 'Uma' and 'Uma-1 '). Appeal preferred by a brother of defendants 5 and 6 therefrom being Title Appeal No. 103 of 1989 was also dismissed. The vested property authority did not take any step against the decree and, as such, the said authority cannot have now anything to say. The trial Court therefore concluded that defendants 5 and 6 could not have any right or interest as lessee under the vested properties authority. It also held that defendant Nos. 5 and 6 failed to prove that they are the heirs of the original recorded tenant, Kashem Ali, Exhibit No. 'Nia'.

22. Thereafter, with regard to the possession, the trial Court found that the plaintiffs paid rents for the suit lands from 1382 BS to 1386 BS by Exhibits No. 5 to 5(Ga) and the defendant 3 paid rents since 1954. The plaintiffs also paid rents for some years intervening. But it reasoned, when PW 1 testified that his father did not possess the land on the basis of sale deed, and that the defendant No. 3 possessed the suit land, and held, the consideration of the testimonies of the' witnesses examined by the plaintiffs on possession was unnecessary. The trial Court also did not give any decision that the defendants 3 or 4 had any right or title in the suit lands.

23. It appears, however, from the judgment of the trial Court that it held solely upon those two statements of PW 1 that as the plaintiffs had no possession in the suit land, so their suit is not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. With regard to the second relief, it found that as in Title Suit No. 264 of 1984 VP Case No. 43 of 1980 was already declared to be illegal and without jurisdiction, and the VP Case is no more effective or binding upon the plaintiffs, so there is no necessity to decide the issue either in favour or against the plaintiffs or defendants.

24. It is my misfortune that I had to consider the judgment of the trial Court elaborately because I could not find any consideration by the appellate Court of the cases of the parties. The appellate Court below just recorded its concurrence with the findings of the trial Court on the issues as framed in the suit, and held that it did not find any reason to differ with the decision of the trial Court on main issues that the plaintiffs could not get any relief and the suit would be dismissed. Before recording its conformance, it did not consider a single document adduced by the parties nor the testimony of any witness. I find the disposal of the appeal did not receive any application of mind of the Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Barisal who heard the appeal. Similarly, he failed to consider the application for amendment of the plaint made on 3-5-1995.

25. I find that the plaintiffs examined- 4 witnesses including a son of original plaintiff, Tayab Ali to prove their case on possession. It is true, there are two statements in the deposition of PW 1 Alfaz Ali, a son of the original plaintiff, Tayeb Ali as recorded which are " আমার বাবা কবলা মূলে দখল করে না"  and   পক্ষভূক্ত তিন নম্বর বিবাদীরা দখল করে” I also find that before the conclusion of his examination- in-chief, PW 1 categorically has denied the suggestions that they did not possess the land and that the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 possess the suit land. Moreover, PW 2 Probhat Chandra Das, who was an employee in the sherista of Kali Mohan Mukherjee proved that Kali Mohan purchased the suit lands in auction, obtained sale certificate and got possession. Then, they annulled the encumbrances by service of notice. He also testified that Kali Mohan transferred the suit lands to Afsar Ali Howlader and Mokter Ali Howlader by a registered sale deed dated 8-6-1962 and Tayeb Ali, original plaintiff purchased the suit lands from said Howladers and possessed. He also identified the signature of Kali Mohan.

26. PW 3 Afsar Ali testified that he and his brother transferred the suit land to Tayeb Ali by a registered deed of sale dated 10-4-1967. They purchased the said lands from Kali Mohan Mukherjee. Tayeb Ali possessed the suit land and after his sons were possessing the said lands. Pw 4 Amjad Khan also testified that Tayeb Ali used to cultivate the suit lands and on his death, his sons were cultivating the said lands.

27. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits before me that in those two sentences PW 1 actually stated that "আমার বাবা কবলা মূলে দখল করে না"  and   পক্ষভূক্ত তিন নম্বর বিবাদীরা দখল করে”  According to him, in the first sentence, the word ''না'' was added and in the second sentence ''না'' was omitted due to mistake. The mistake would be apparent if the entire evidence of the PW 1 and those of other PW s on the question of possession are read and considered. He also submits that the petitioners could learn about the mistake only after taking a copy of the judgment in order to prefer an appeal and they had no opportunity to seek any correction before the trial Court.

28. I find, the trial court read those two lines only and allowed itself to be swayed away. It did not conceal its mind by saying that in view of those statements, consideration of the evidence of other witnesses was not necessary. It should be mentioned that the trial court considered the series of documents of title and also the rent receipts adduced by the plaintiffs. It did not find anything against the documents. But it preferred not to draw any conclusion on the title from those documents, as it found the plaintiffs were not in possession on the basis of those statements of PW 1 only.

29. It has already been stated above that the appe1late court did not consider any evidence at all. Rather, the appellate court rejected the application for amendment as irrelevant for consideration that as the mistake in recording the deposition of PW 1 as mentioned in the application was not raised before the trial court at the proper time.

30. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners deserve serious consideration. It is true, the parties are litigating since long after the institution of the suit on 28-12-1981. In exercise of the jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, I am afraid, I can decide the pertinent question whether there was any such mistake during recording the statement of PW 1 Alfaz Ali, and if the answer is in the positive, then whether the application of the plaintiffs for amendment of the plaint should be allowed or not. If the case is a fit case for remand then where to send The learned Advocate for the opposite party requests for remand to the appellate court, in view of the delay.

<u>31. I have already found that the appellate court did not consider any evidence on record nor gave its own decision on the question of title and possession. Moreover, it is the trial court which, can effectively dispose of the application for amendment of the plaint. If the application is found to be fit to allow the plaintiffs to add the prayer for confirmation of possession on payment of proper court fees, then, it can also allow the defendants to file additional written statement, if they so desire. There may be a necessity for additional evidence to be adduced by the parties for determining the real question in controversy between the parties.</u>

32. I have also considered the cases cited by the learned Advocate. In the case of Nawab Ali Dhakua vs Abdur Rashid and others, (1994) 14 BLD (AP) 229, the suit for deciaration of title and confirmation of possession was dismissed by the trial Court and on appeal, this Division dismissed the appeal and affirmed the decision of the trial court. In further appeal before the Appellate Division, it was held that

"The importance of considering the evidence independently cannot be over-emphasised and the appellate judgment must reflect such consideration but in the case of affirming of the findings of the trial court, the narration of the entire evidence and reiteration of the reasons given by the trial court are not essential but expressions of general agreement with those of the trial court and proving additional reasons, if any, are generally considered sufficient. Expression of general agreement with reasons given by the court decision of which is under appeal would ordinarily suffice. In case of reversal of a finding of fact, however, the consideration of the evidence of necessity, has to be thorough and more elaborate. This case has no manner of application to the facts of the case. Rather, here, the judgment of the appellate court is based on total non-consideration of the evidence on record and absence of any finding of its own. In view of provisions of Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, such judgment must be held to be no judgment at all in the eye of law."

33. In the case of Abdul Mannan and others vs Akram Ali and others, 43 DLR (AD) 125, the suit for deciaration of title on the basis of settlement from the landlords was dismissed by the trial court but on appeal the appellate court allowed the appeal and decreed the suit finding the title and possession of the plaintiffs. In revision therefrom, this Division set aside the judgment of the appellate court and sent back the suit to the trial court on remand being of the view that finding of title of the plaintiff by the appellate court was based on misreading of the evidence on record particularly, the rent receipts. In further appeal, the Appellate Division allowed the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and directed this Division to dispose of the revision applications on merit on the joint prayer of the learned Counsels on the ground that the entire evidence, both oral and documentary, was available on record and there was no necessity for remand. This case also does not support the opposite party.

34. Under Order VI rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court may at any stage of the proceedings allow either party to alter or amend his pleadings ill. such a manner and on such terms as may be just and all such amendments shall be made as may be necessary for the purpose of determining the real question-in controversy between the parties.

35. In Golam Hafez Mia vs Khadem Ali Meah, 29 DLR (AD) 311, in a suit for declaration, the trial court found the plaintiff was in possession of the suit lands. But the first appellate court reversed the finding and found the defendant in possession and accordingly, held that the suit was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act in the absence of a prayer for consequential relief. In second appeal, a prayer was made before this Division to allow the plaintiff, to amend his plaint by adding the prayer for recovery of possession, but it was refused and the appeal was dismissed. In further appeal before the Appellate Division, the prayer was allowed by the Appellate Division and the suit was remitted back to the trial court for allowing the plaintiff to amend the pleading by adding the prayer for recovery of possession on payment of proper court fees. The defendant was also given opportunity to file additional written statement. The trial court was directed to decide the question of recovery of possession and ancillary question of adverse possession of the defendant if so raised. The court was also given the liberty to allow the parties to adduce additional evidence, if the parties so pray and the court thinks fit to allow.

36. For the reasons stated above, in my judgment, the case should be sent back on remand to the trial court.

In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgments and decrees of both the courts below are set aside. The case is sent back on remand to the court of Assistant Judge at Barisal. The court shall consider the application for amendment of the-plaint for adding a prayer for confirmation of possession. If the prayer is allowed, the court would be at liberty to allow the defendants to file additional written statement, if any, they want to. Then, the court would decide finally all the questions at issue between the parties afresh in accordance with law and in the light of the above observations, if necessary, on further evidence as may be adduced by the parties. The court would abide by the ultimate result of the suit.

End.

lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam with Md Abdul Alim Miah, Samarendra Nath Biswas Advocates ----- For the Petitioners
AF Hasan Ariff Attorney-General with Farah Mahbub, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the Respondents
parties:
Abdur Rahman (Md) & another ------ Petitioners
vs
Government of Bangladesh hand ors   ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed Refaat Ahmed J: In this Application under Article 102 of the Constitution a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Notice issued in Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 2002-2003 by the respondent No. 3 (as contained in Annexure-'1') shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and or such order or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The case of the petitioner is that three individuals being sons of late Hari Prashanna Ghosh filed a suit being Other Suit No. 216 of 1975 against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (as principal defendant) and others on 2-10-1975 for a decree declaring their title in 0.20 acres of land of CS Plot No. 3600 of Mouza Botardia. In that suit the three plaintiffs stated that their predecessor Hari Prashanna Ghosh got settlement of the suit land from the landlord but that in the SA Khatian the said land was wrongly recorded in the name of the Government and that as a result they were compelled to file the said suit. The CS Plot No. 3600 was a big plot and in the SA Record the same has been recorded in several SA Plots. The land that was taken by way of settlement by the predecessor of the three plaintiffs was recorded in SA Plot No. 1730 with an area of 20 acre In the course of the said suit there was a Commission to ascertain whether SA Plot No. 1730 is a part of CS Plot No. 3600 and the Advocate Commissioner in his report stated that SA Plot No. 1730 has been created out of the land of CS Plot No. 3600 (Annexure-'B'). The petitioners state that the plaintiff in the said suit filed unregistered do Amalnama in evidence of settlement of the suit land and on the basis of the same the suit was decreed on 28-4-78 declaring the plaintiffs' right, title and interest in the suit land (Annexures-'C' and 'C(1)'). Thereafter; one of the three plaintiffs in the suit; Sunil Kumar Ghosh, the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners, mutated his name in Miscellaneous Case No.20 of 1978-1979 in respect of 0.0667 acre of the suit land and paid rent for the same. The petitioners have annexed the Mutation Khatian in the name of the said Sunil Kumar Ghosh; duplicate carbon receipt showing payment of separation fees and rent receipt under Annexures 'D', 'D(1)' and 'D(2)' respectively. The petitioners state that it is this 0.0667 of acre of land from the SA Plot No. 1730 which was purchased by them from Sunil Kumar Ghosh by a registered deed of sale dated 20- 2-1996 (Annexure-'E'). Thereafter, the petitioners filed Mutation Case No. 1038 of 1995-96 and accordingly, their names were mutated on 21-8-1996 (Annexure-'F'). The petitioners have annexed receipts of separation fees and rent paid in the Annexure-'G' series of the Writ Petition. This was followed by an approval of a construction plan by the Sirajanj Pourashava on 2-1-2000 for the construction of a three-storied building on the purchased land. It is now the petitioners contention that purely as a device for harassment the Tahshildar of the office of the respondent No. 3 Assistant Commissioner of Land, Sirajganj filed an application for cancellation of the petitioners mutation allowed in Mutation Case No. 1038 of 1995-1996 as obtained on the basis of Title Suit No. 216 of 1975. The petitioners contend, that this device is evident in the impugned notice in Annexure-'H' putting the petitioners on notice of the commencement of Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 2002-2003 and requiring the petitioners appearance before the concerned authority on 10-11-2002. The petitioners submit that the impugned notice is illegal as the name of their predecessor-in-interest was mutated in Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 1978-79 on the basis of the decree in Other Suit No. 216 of 1975 and that the petitioners names have thereafter been mutated as transferees through Mutation Case No. 1038 of 1995-96. Further, a building having already been constructed on the land in question, the petitioners now fear and apprehend a possible demolition of that construction as a probable consequence' of the issuance of the impugned notice in Annexure-'1'.

3. In response, the respondent No.1 has stated that the Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 2002-2003 has been initiated on the primary ground that false and forged documents created by the petitioners have constituted the basis of the petitioners Mutation Case No. 1038 of 1995-1996. In this regard, it is the contention of the respondent No.1 that a canal was excavated approximately three hundred years ago over CS Plot No. 3600, of which the land in question constitutes a part, along with its adjacent area of Bhuterdiar Mouza in PS Sirajganj, District Pabna (now, Sirajganj) and the said canal- river flows from north to south measuring 25 Km in length touching the Jamuna river on both ends of the canal, thereby contending that the petitioners land is originally a part of the canal excavated for navigational purpose. The respondent No. 1 shows that the land in CS Plot No. 3600 is situated within two CS Khatians, ie CS Khatian Nos. 341 and 337 and identified therein as Baral River for use by the general public Annexures-' A' and 'A(1)' respectively of the Affidavit-in-Opposition filed on behalf of the respondent No.1). The respondent No.1 also contends that during SA operation the canal recorded in Plot No. 1730 with an area of 5,7125 acres of land along with other plots in Bhuterdiar Mouza in PS Sirajganj was recorded in the name of zamindars of different estates and shown in SA Khatian No. 235 as Baral River as "used by the general public" (Annexure-'B' to the Affidavit-in- Opposition). In this regard, it is also the contention of the respondent No.1 that the said SA Record was wrongly prepared in the name of the zamindars and their heirs. The respondent No.1 draws a picture of a gradual and sustained encroachment into the canal area over a period of many years by unscrupulous persons and, in that context, states that the then landlord never settled the River Plot No. 3600 to Hari Prashanna Ghosh at any date through patina or by any other means and that any assertion of the existence of such pattani is to be deemed as false, collusive, concocted and not acted upon.

4. The respondent No.1 also puts this Court on notice of a large development scheme undertaken by the Sirajganj Pourashava to re-excavate the old Katakhali river with a view to making Sirajganj a model town by improving its ecological environment. In that regard, steps have already been taken to require illegal occupants to vacate lands in CS Plot No. 3600 and to hand over the possession of the occupied lands to the respondents. It is in this context that the impugned notice was issued, the respondent No.1 stating that the notice reflects the mere initiation of a process to ascertain facts and questions of title and is a direction to show cause and is by no means to be treated as a final order.

5. Heard the Learned Counsel for the petitioner, and the Learned Attorney-General, perused the Writ Petition and the Supplementary Affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners, the Affidavit-in-Opposition filed on behalf of the respondent No.1, the petitioners Affidavit-in-Reply and the annexures.

<u>6. Upon a consideration and perusal of statements and documents presented before this Court, it is evident to this Court that issues as raised therein pertain primarily to disputed questions of fact as regards survey records and the details therein. This is reflected not only in the assertion above made by the respondent No.1 of the possibility of error in the preparation of the relevant SA Record but it is also evident in the petitioners' contention in their Affidavit-in-Reply that CS Plot No. 3600 was neither a canal nor was it locally referred to as Katakhali river, but rather that the same was owned and possessed by the landlord as a low-lying area notwithstanding which it was wrongly recorded in both the CS and SA Khatians as a river. The issue of disputed and contradictory question of fact and title also arise in the petitioners' statements in the Affidavit-in-Reply that the landlord had already settled the case plot to different persons before the SA Record, but that in the said Record that plot was wrongly shown to be held by the former landlord instead of the subsequent transferee. In the view of this Court, and considered in the facts and circumstances of this case, these inconsistent and conflicting questions of both facts and title fall outside the purview of assessment in Writ Jurisdiction.</u>

<u>7. In this context the Learned Attorney- General Mr Hasan Ariff has submitted that there was reasonable basis for the issuance of the impugned notice in Annexure-'1' under section 150 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act'). The Learned Attorney-General has submitted that the validity of the impugned notice could, however, indeed be challenged by the petitioner under the relevant provisions on revision of section 149 of the Act, but this the petitioners opted not to do. Failing that, it is evident to this Court that this application has been filed primarily out of an apprehension or fear of a future contingency of a possible demolition of the construction on the said plot. In that context, it is not clear to this Court the extent to which the issuance of the impugned notice in Annexure-'1' constitutes a violation of the petitioners' fundamental rights that can be challenged in Writ Jurisdiction. This Court, in agreement with the submission of the Learned Attorney-General to that effect, notes that the petitioners appear to be saying that they have a legal right not to be saddled with the impugned notice and that the respondent No.3 is under a corresponding legal duty not to issue the said notice or is not competent to issue the same. This Court is inclined to hold that in the facts and circumstances of this case there is nothing to substantiate that position adopted by the petitioners. This Court, therefore, finds that the impugned notice in Annexure-'1' is valid as having been made with lawful authority. Accordingly, this Court is of the view that it would be best for the petitioners to pursue the matter as raised in the impugned notice through the process and the proper forum reflected in the said impugned notice.</u>

8. In light of the above this Court finds no substance in this Rule.

9. In the result the Rule is discharged. Pending proper and final disposal of the case as initiated by the impugned notice and upon due opportunity given to the petitioners to be heard and to submit their case, the respondents are hereby directed not to disturb in any manner the petitioner's peaceful possession of the said plot in question and the existing structure constructed thereon. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of this Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

There is no order as to costs.

End.

lawyer:
Sk Afralur Rahman, Advocate  ----- For the Petitioner. 
Shamim Khaled Ahmed, Advocate  ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Shankar Lal Das ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Janata Bank & others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: The above Rule was obtained by the judgment debtor upon making an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against order No. 101 dated 11-8-94 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court at Mymensingh in Officer in Charge Execution Case No. 8 of 1993 by which the prayer for dismissal of the execution case after adjustment of decretal debt was rejected, and the mortgaged properties were ordered to be sold by public auction.

2. In the application, it is stated that on 8-9-82 opposite party No. 1, the Bank as plaintiff instituted Mortgage Suit No. 116 of 1982 against the petitioner for recovery of a sum of Taka 2,57,130.30 for his failure in the repayment on the bank loan under a cash credit account. On the prayer of the plaintiff, on the same day, two trucks of the petitioner (already hypothecated to the Bank in connection with separate loan) and the house property of the judgment debtor were attached under the provisions of order XXXVIII rule 5 of the Code, and also a warrant of arrest was issued against the petitioner and his wife, opposite party No. 2. In the circumstances, the Bank on 13-9-82 obtained a compromise executed by the petitioner and thereupon, on 16-9-82 obtained a final decree upon such compromise from the Court.

3. As per terms of the compromise decree, Mr Jamshed Ali, Advocate stood surety to the debt of the judgment debtor, and he was appointed the receiver.

4. On 31-8-83 at the instance of the Bank Officer in Charge Execution Case No. 8 of 1983 was started, Before the executing Court, the Bank made an application for a direction upon the receiver to furnish an account of last 14 months and to deposit the income in the Bank and also for change of the receiver on various allegations against the receiver. On 11-7-84 the receiver filed a written objection to the prayer and also submitted an account in Court. The matter was ultimately heard on 12-1-85 when the executing Court allowed the prayer of the Bank, changed the receiver and asked the Bank to take possession of the trucks, and ordered to issue sale proclamations for sale of the trucks and the house property by public auction.

5. An application of opposite party No. 2 dated 15-8-84 made under section 151 of the Code for setting aside the compromise decree on ground of fraud was also rejected by the executing Court by its order dated 11-8-85.

6. Eventually, on 13-2-85 truck being of reg. No. Mymensingh Na. 239 was seized by the police and on 16-2-85 other truck reg. No. Dhaka Na. 1737 was handed over to the Bank by its driver.

7. Against the order, the petitioner unsuccessfully moved this Division in Civil Revision No. 82 of 1982 and the Appellate Division in CP No. 28 of 1990.

8. Then, on 27-8-90 the petitioner made an application before the executing Court for return of the trucks after adjustment of the decretal dues out of the income of the trucks from the period 12-1-85 to 25-8-90. It was claimed in the application that on the showing of the Bank, the trucks were earning Taka 1000 daily and the Bank might have earned about Taka 40,46,000 during the period. The amount was far greater than the decretal debt. Yet the Bank was not returning the trucks. Rather, the Bank was trying to sell the trucks and the landed properties mortgaged. At the time, the price of Truck-Mymensingh Na-239 of British Bedford chassis would be Taka ten lac while that of Truck Dhaka Na-1737 of Hindusthan Motors chassis would be seven lac.

9. The decree holder Bank did not file any written objection to the application. But it produced some papers in support of its case that the crankshaft of Truck, Na-239 was broken the truck was so received from the police. The truck was kept in Salam Motors for repair. Driver of Dhaka Na. 1737 did not hand over to the Bank the Blue Book and Road Permit of the truck. On 17-2-85 the Bank applied before the executing Court for direction upon the receiver for handing over the Blue Book and Road Permit. As the Bank could not get said papers, the truck could not be run. It is also the case of the Bank that the Bank did not earn any money out of the trucks.

10. The application was heard on 11-8-94. Hearing the parties, the executing Court was of the view that the petitioner failed to prove that the trucks were handed over to the Bank in good and running condition and the Bank was allowed to run and earn income out of the trucks and also that the application made under Order XXI rule 19 of the Code was not maintainable. Upon such view of the matter, the executing Court rejected the application by impugned judgment and order and ordered for sale of mortgaged house property.

11. An affidavit-in-opposition filed on behalf of the decree holder Bank further states that meanwhile Suit No. 219 of 1985 and Suit No. 220 of 1985 were also instituted by the Bank against the petitioner for recovery of loan advanced for purchase of the trucks and on 20-9-86 both the suits were decreed ex parte. Miscellaneous cases brought by the petitioner against the ex parte decrees also failed. Miscellaneous appeals preferred therefrom were also dismissed.

12. The decree holder Bank having applied for execution of the decrees Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 and No.3 of 1989 commenced. But further proceedings of the cases remained stayed in the Rules obtained by the petitioner in Civil Rule No. 45 of 1990 and No. 46 of 1990 until 1989. After the disposal of the Rules, the Bank obtained steps in the execution proceedings and the executing Court vide order No. 49 dated 6-1-91 ordered for analogous execution of execution case Nos. 2 and 3 of 1989 with execution case No. 8 of 1983. It is submitted thereupon that the revision application involves decision on disputed questions of fact, resolution of which is not possible and the Rule is therefore liable to be discharged.

13. Few facts that are not disputed need to be restated in order to appreciate the decision of the executing Court dated 11-8-94 in rejecting the application of the petitioner. On 8-9-82 opposite party No. 1, the Bank instituted Mortgage Suit. No.116 of 1982 against the petitioner for recovery of a sum of Taka 2,57,130.30 on account of cash credit. Same day, on the prayer of the plaintiff, two trucks of the petitioner (already hypothecated to the Bank in connection with separate loans) and the house property of the judgment debtor were attached, and also a warrant of arrest was issued against the petitioner and his wife, opposite party No.2. In such circumstances, the Bank filed in Court a compromise dated 13-9-82 executed by the petitioner and thereupon, on 16-9-82 obtained a final decree upon such compromise from the Court.

The compromise decree contains the following amongst other terms,

a.	suit was finally decreed for the sum with the interest and costs as prayed for;

b.	the judgment debtor would satisfy the entire debt under the decree with interest and costs by deposit of the decreed money in 4 equal installments in the Bank on proper receipt;

c.	the attachment would continue till satisfaction of the decreed sum; and the attached two trucks would be placed under the custody of a receiver to be appointed by the Court and the receiver would deposit the income of the trucks towards the satisfaction of the trucks.

14. In a mortgage suit, it may be noted, such final decree could only be passed after the accounts taken and for a specified balance, if any due. In spite of such final decree, record shows that a preliminary decree was drawn and signed on 26-9-82. In preliminary decree the above terms and conditions, amongst others, were restated only. The decree holder on the basis of its own account applied for execution for a sum of Taka 2,57,130.30 as principal and interest on said principal at the rate of 20% from the period of 1-7-82 to 28-8-83. Thereafter, on 1-12-83 the decree holder Bank made an application for amendment of the execution for deduction of Taka 60,000 as received by the Bank from the receiver from the principal and the executing Court allowed the same by its order dated 8-1-1984. The Court also asked the receiver to submit the accounts. The record does not show any final decree, as such, was made on the basis of any accounts whatsoever after such preliminary decree.

15. Meanwhile, on the application of the Bank dated 27-11-83 and the objection of the receiver dated 11-7-84 along with the accounts supported by vouchers, the executing Court by its order 12-1-85 allowed the prayer of the Bank, changed the receiver and asked the Bank to take possession of the trucks, and ordered to issue sale proclamations for sale of the trucks and the house property by public auction. It may be mentioned that in his report, the receiver claimed to have deposited Taka 72,000. The receiver also stated to have received Taka 80,584 from the judgment debtor, petitioner for purchase of 8 tyres for the trucks. The accounts show that during the period from 26-9-82 to 30-6-84 the truck. Dhaka Na-1737 earned Taka 3,08,080 while Mymensingh Na-239 Taka 3,45,070.

16. It is also not disputed that on 13-2-85 the truck of reg. No. Mymensingh Na-239 was seized by the police and 16-2-85 other Truck of reg. No. Dhaka Na-1737 was handed over to the Bank by its driver. The Bank then took delivery of the earlier truck from the police.

17. In the application dated 27-11-83, the Bank stated on the conditions of the trucks as hereunder.

"that the schedule below attached trucks are in good and running conditions the minimum income of which is not less than Taka 1,000 (one thousand) each day, but the receiver in connivance with the jdr. has deposited Taka 60,000 (sixty thousand) only within the period of last 14 months and that the receiver being biased and illegally has also handed over the trucks to jdr. and the said trucks are under absolute control of the jdr. at present which may frustrate and even make the decree infructuous. "

18. After taking possession of the trucks, the decree holder Bank on 14-2-85 made an application for an order asking the receiver for handing over of necessary papers of the truck and the receiver also prayed for time. The executing Court stayed further proceedings of the executing case on wrong view that this Division granted stay in Civil Revision No. 82 of 1985 against order dated 12-1-85; in fact, operation of the order was stayed only. However, the decree holder did take no steps whatsoever either to run the trucks or to repair or to sell them if those were beyond repair. Now Mr Shamim wants us to believe that the trucks have over the years turned into junk. If it is so, the decree holder Bank cannot evade the consequence-the liability for the loss of the trucks. The decree holder Bank must be held accountable, at least for the worth of the trucks as on 16-2-85 when they took delivery of them and the judgment debtor will be entitled to adjustment to the extent of the price of the trucks as on that date.

<u>19. Moreover, we find that in execution case No. 2 of 1989 the proclamation was issued for sale of 0.05 1/3 acre of land of SA plot No. 2334 appertaining to SA Khatian No. 821 and CS Khatian No. 821 and in execution case No. 3 of 1989, in addition to said land, another land measuring 10 decimals out of 43 decimals of plot No. 2555 appertaining to Khatian No. 330 for recover of Taka 1,50,000 in each execution. Land of plot No. 2555, it is submitted by Mr Afzalur Rahman for the petitioner, was never attached. On the other hand, the order attaching the land of plot No. 1334 shows that there are godown, shop and house situate on the land. The proclamation does neither contain full particulars of the nature of property nor the probable market price of the property. The law is settled that in the absence of such particulars, no valid order for proclamation for sale could be made.</u>

20. In the circumstances, the application of the petitioner dated 27-8-90 deserved consideration. But the executing Court wholly misconceived the purport of the application and rejected the same both technically as well as on merit. The executing Court was, on the above facts, wrong to hold that the petitioner failed to prove that the trucks were handed over to the decree holder Bank in good and running condition and that the Bank was allowed by the Court to earn income out of the trucks. Firstly, the findings of the Court are not borne out by the record and secondly, the judgment debtor was under no obligation to prove the conditions under which the decree holder Bank got the custody of the trucks from the receiver i.e. from the custody of the Court.

<u>21. Lastly, the executing Court was right to find the application as made under Order XXI rule 19 of the Code is not maintainable for the petitioner as a judgment debtor cannot maintain such an application for legal set-off. But the provisions of Order XXI rules 18 and 19 of the Code must not be taken as exhaustive. The claim of the petitioner is based on equity and the petitioner is therefore entitled to an equitable set-off. We find the view we have taken is supported by a decision of a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court in the case of Bank of Dacca Ltd vs Gour Gopal Saha, AIR 1936 Calcutta 409 and that of a Full Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court in the case of B Sheshaiah vs Veerabhadrayya, AIR 1972 Andhra Pradesh 134. The ratio decidendi of the cases is that on general principles and in the exercise of its inherent power, an executing Court can entertain and give effect to a claim to set-off even in cases which do not come strictly under Order XXI rule 19 of the Code. And equitable set-off can be claimed in a case where cross-demands arise out of the same transaction as well as in cases where the cross-demands may not arise out of the same transaction but they are so connected in the nature of circumstances that it would be inequitable to allow one party to execute his decree driving the other party to separate suit or proceedings. Granting of set-off however rests entirely with the discretion of the Court. No party, of course, as of right can claim such set-off. It is needless to say that the discretion is to be exercised judicially. In such view of the matter, the execution Court is obliged to investigate the claim of the judgment debtor for adjustment.</u>

22. In the circumstances and in view of the above legal position, the impugned order of the executing Court cannot be sustained in law. The matter should be sent back to the executing Court for investigation of the claim of the judgment debtor for the ends of justice.

23. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without however any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 11-8-94 are set aside. The executing Court is hereby directed to investigate the claim of the judgment debtor for adjustment, and ascertain the amount so far received from him or out of the income of the trucks on the basis of the accounts submitted by the receiver, and also the price of the trucks as on 16-2-85. After deductions of the receipts and the price of the trucks, if any balance is found due from the judgment debtor, the execution will only proceed to recover the amount in accordance with law.

Send down the records at once.

End.

lawyer:
Abdul Hamid with Md. Abdul Majid, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner 
Md. Nazibur Rahman with Marfat Ali and AH Mustafizur Rahman, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Party Nos. 1 (b) and 1 (d).
parties:
Abdul Khaleque (Md) ------ Petitioner
vs.
Raj Mohammad Sarker and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the defendant- petitioner is against judgment and decree dated 24.4.80 passed by Subordinate Judge, Dinajpur in Title Appeal No. 75 of 1977 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30.6.77 passed by the Munsif, 2nd Court Dinajpur in Title Suit No. 367 of 1968.

2. Opposite party No. 1 and Abdul Majid Predecessor of opposite party Nos. 2-13 as plaintiffs filed on 1.12.62 Title Suit No. 176 of 1962 against the petitioner and another for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit property measuring .22 acres of plot No. 372/1065 of khatian No. 614 situated within Kalitala of Dinajpur town with structures standing thereon and the said suit subsequently was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 367 of 1968.

3. Case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that 4 sisters-Prova Rani, Shoba Rani, Santi Moyee and Sudha Moyee-were the owners of the suit property and other properties and subsequently Sudha Moyee died leaving her three sisters who exchanged the suit property along with other properties with Indian properties of the plaintiffs by executing power of attorney dated 20.4.61 Ext. 1 and exchange kabala Ext. 2 executed on 10.4.62 and registered on 11.1.62 in their favour: that plaintiffs got possession in the other lands on the basis of the said exchange except the suit property which was in illegal occupation of defendant No. 1 since 1958 and he inducted defendant No. 2 therein in 1960: that plaintiffs demanded possession from the defendants but they having delayed to amicably vacate the suit property plaintiffs sent a notice to deft. No. 1 through their Advocate on 10.5.62 to vacate the suit property and he received the same on 17.5.62; that defendants having not amicably vacated the suits property plaintiffs filed the suit with the aforesaid prayer. After the suit came on remand plaintiffs added Shamapada, husband of Prova Rani; Assistant Custodian and Government of Bangladesh as defendants and also added paragraph 6 in the plaint asserting that Karimati Debi, mother of plaintiffs' vendors obtained a deed of relinquishment on 6.8.33 from her 3 daughters in her favour in respect of the suit property and gifted the' same to her daughter Prova Rani and her husband Shyama Pada Chakraborty by way of dower for giving her in marriage to the said Shyamapada Chakraborty by registered deed but the said deeds were never acted upon and the 3 sisters continued in title and possession of the same.

4. Defendant No. 2 did not contest the suit. He filed a petition of compromise admitting title of the plaintiffs in the suit property and making over possession of the huts occupied by him to the plaintiffs. But the defendant No. 1 contested the suit denying all material allegations and asserting that Shyama Charan Chakraborty became the owner of the suit property on the basis of gift from his mother-in-law Harimati Debi and the said Shyama Charan Chakraborty possessed the suit property by recording his name in the municipal assessment register and paying taxes and rents and letting out the same to monthly bharatias including Durga Prasanna Chaterjee; that though the name of Proba Rani was included in the deed of .gift she was merely a benamder of Shyama Charan; that Prova Rani and her other sisters never owned and possessed the suit property; that one Azizur Rahman was caretaker of the said house after partition of the country in 1947; that defendant No. 1 came to Dinajpur in 1950 with members of his family and took shelter in the suit property; that defendant No. 1 got his name recorded in the present settlement operation but due to objection by the plaintiffs his name was omitted; that Shyama Charan Chakravorty entered into an agreement with the defendant No. 1 on 2.2.50 to sell the suit property along with another property at a consideration of Taka 22,000.00 and received Taka 500.00 &5 advance; that as Shyama Charan left for India he could not execute and register sale deed in favour of defendant No. 1 on receipt of balance of the consideration money; that the suit is barred by limitation and as such that same should be dismissed.

5. Upon the aforesaid pleadings and evidence adduced by parties both oral and documentary trial Court by judgment dated 10.12.68 decreed the suit in part granting joint possession to the plaintiffs with defendant No. 1. On appeal by the plaintiffs suit was remanded and after remand the plaint was amended and by judgment dated 30.6.77 trial Court decreed the suit in full. Being aggrieved by the same defendant No.1 preferred appeal which was dismissed by the impugned judgment dated 24.4.80. Being aggrieved by the same petitioner obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr. Abdul Hamid, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner after placing the judgments of both the Court below and other materials on records, submitted that Court of appeal below acted illegally in passing the impugned judgment without considering that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession and dispossession within 12 years of filing of the suit. He further submitted that in spite of petitioner's adducing evidence both oral and documentary in support of his adverse possession since January, 1950 Court of appeal below acted illegally in not holding that the petitioner acquired title in the suit property by adverse possession.

7. Trial Court in deciding issue regarding limitation and title on consideration of evidence came to the conclusion that the suit is not barred by limitation as the suit has been filed on 1.12.62 within 12 years of the petition's entering in the suit premises on 11.4.52 and that plaintiffs acquired title in the suit premises by exchange kabala dated 10.1.62 Ext.2 executed and registered on the basis of a power of attorney Ext. 1 executed by the 3 sisters who were the owners of the suit property as the deed of relinquishment and gift in question were never acted upon and that bainapatra in favour of defendant No.1 was forged and ante-dated.

8. It appears from the judgment of the Court of appeal below that the Court of appeal below concurred with the finding of the trial Court that the deed of agreement Ext. F is not a genuine document but reversed the finding of the trial Court that the deed of gift Ext. 8 in favour of Prova Rani and her husband Shyama Pada Chakraborty was never acted upon. Court of appeal below further found that the defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit premises from 1956 and, as such, the suit is not barred by limitation and plea of adverse possession cannot be entertained. Court of appeal below again found that Prova Rani and her husband Shyama Pada Chakraborty became owners of the suit property on the basis of deed of gift Ext.8 but avoided the difficulty of plaintiffs' acquiring title in /16/-annas share of the suit property relying on the fact that Shyama Pada Chakraborty, husband of Prova Rani did not challenge plaintiffs' claim of title in the entire suit property though he was impleaded in the suit and summons of the suit was served upon him.

9. Plaintiffs' case is that their vendors left the suit property in 1952 keeping the same vacant and defendant No.1 entered into the same in 1958 and he inducted defendant No. 1 in 1960. On the other hand, the case of the contesting defendant is that he entered into the suit property in January, 1950 finding the same vacant when one Azizur Rahman who was the caretaker of that house objected but ultimately remained silent and he obtained a refugee certificate from the Secretary Anjuman-e-Mohajerin. On consideration of the said certificate Ext. 'B' trial Court found that the same was issued on 11.4.52 and, as such, came to the conclusion that the suit filed on 1.12.62 was not barred by limitation. Court of appeal below on consideration of the municipal assessments register Ext. L (1) for the period 1946-1950 found that one Durgapada was bharatia in the suit premises under Shyamapada Chakraborty. On consideration of another assessment register for the period 1951-55 Ext. L(2) the said Court found that Santosh was bharatia in the said premises under Shyamapada Chakraborty. On consideration of subsequent assessment registers from 1956 onwards Ext. L (3) and L (4) the said Court found that the defendant No.1 has been possessing the suit premises since 1956. So it held that the suit having been filed in 1962, within 12 years from 1956 is neither barred by limitation nor defendant No. 1 acquired any title by adverse possession in the suit premises. Court of appeal below also considered the deed of agreement Ext. F and concurred with the finding of the trial Court that the same is forged and, therefore, did not rely upon the same to support petitioner's claim of adverse possession.

10. In view of the aforesaid documentary evidence Court of appeal below did not rely only the oral evidence of DWs after considering the same as the oral evidence was contrary to the aforesaid documentary evidence. It is well settled that oral evidence contrary to undisputed documentary evidence cannot be relied on. Oral evidence can be used to connect and explain undisputed documentary evidence. Court of appeal below relied on the municipal assessment registers Ext. 'L' series produced by the defendant and rightly rejected oral testimony of the DWs contrary to the same. Therefore, I do not find any illegality on the part of the Court of appeal below in concluding that the suit is not barred by limitation and petitioner did not acquire title in the suit property by adverse possession.

11. It is the admitted case of both the parties that the suit premise was vacant after the owners left the same. It is further case of the defendant-petitioner that the suit premises was lying vacant under the care of one Azizur Rahman and he objected at the time of petitioner's entering into the premises. So long as the property remained vacant it was, presumed to be in possession of the rightful owners. Therefore, admittedly suit property was in possession of the vendors of the plaintiffs till the petitioner entered therein. Therefore, it can be safely concluded that plaintiffs' vendors were in possession of the suit premises till 1956 when the petitioner entered into the suit premises without paying heed to the objection of the said caretaker Azizur Rahman. Plaintiffs’ having filed the suit on 1.12.62 within 12 years of dispossession of their vendors in 1956 by the petitioner, the suit is not barred by limitation.

<u>12. Before parting with the judgment it is necessary to consider an intricate question of law as to whether a co-sharer can recover possession of the property from a trespasser, Court of appeal below on consideration of deed of gift Ext. 8, municipal assessment registers Ext. 'L' series and CS Khatian Ext. E (3) recording suit property in the possession of Prova Rani found that Shyama Pada Chakravorty and Prova Rani acquired right, title and possession in the suit property. Admittedly Shyamapada Chakravorty did not execute the power of attorney Ext. 'I' on the basis of which the deed of exchange kabala Ext.2 was executed and registered. Court of appeal below obviated this difficulty by noticing that Shyama Pada Chakarborty did not challenge plaintiffs' claim of title in the entire suit property in spite of being impleaded and served with summons of the suit. Even if it is found that plaintiffs acquired title of Prova Rani only on the basis of Ext. l and 2 in the suit premises defendant petitioner having been found to be a rank trespasser in the suit premises and he having not acquired any title by adverse possession plaintiffs are entitled to recover khas possession of the suit premises by evicting the petitioner. In this respect reliance can be made in the cases of Md. Abdur Rahman Bhuiyan vs. Prajulla Chandra Majumdar reported in PLD 1963 (Dhaka) 57; Fazal Hussain vs. Noor Khan reported in PLD 1957 (Lah) 43; Ram Charan vs. Bansidhar and others reported in AIR 1942 (All) 358 and RN Das vs. Loknath Mandai reported in AIR 1970 Patna l (FB). In the aforesaid cases it has been consistently held that a suit at the instance of a co-sharer against a trespasser for recovery of possession is maintainable without even impleading the other co-sharers. In this case after remand Shyama Pada Chakraborty was impleaded and it has already been noticed that he did not contest the claim of the plaintiffs. Vested property authority and Government also did not contest the claim of the plaintiffs though impleaded in this suit. In the above facts and circumstances I find no illegality in the impugned judgment and decree to interfere with the same.</u>

In the result, the Rule is discharged with cost.

End.
