SS Halder, Mir Mokhlesur Rahman, Advocates ----- For the Defendant Opposite Parties.
parties:
Sharif Ullah Patwary and others ------ Petitioner
vs.
Jharna Dhara Chowdhury and another ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J: This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioners is against the judgment and order dated 19.11.86 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Noakhali in Miscellaneous Case No. 141 of 1983.

2. The petitioner Nos. 1, 3-5 and late Ali Azam, the predecessor-in-interest of petitioner Nos. 2(a) to 2(i) as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 706/81 on 23.12.81 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Noakhali for declaration of their title by adverse possession in the suit land measuring 27.73 acres against the opposite parties and others. The suit was decreed on compromise against defendant Nos. 1-3 and ex parte against other defendants including the opposite parties on 28.8.82. Thereafter on 14.7.83 the opposite parties filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree and upon the said application Miscellaneous Case No.141/83 was registered on 9.4.84 after receipt of the record from the Record Room.

3. Opposite-parties herein filed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case for setting aside the ex parte decree against them on the allegations, inter alia that the summons of the suit were not served upon them and the plaintiffs suppressed the same by unduly influencing the process server and obtained a false return of service in collusion with their own men as attesting witnesses. Had the defendants an opportunity to contest the suit, the suit could not have been decreed and the plaintiffs in collusion with their party men defendant Nos. 1-3 filed a fraudulent petition of compromise; that it is apparent from the return of the service of summons that the same were not served and have been suppressed; that the defendant-petitioners opposite parties herein did not know about the said ex parte decree and when plaintiff No.1 threatened the present opposite party No. 2 on 16.6.83 saying that they should not enter into the suit property as he obtained a decree of perpetual injunction and after hearing the same defendant-petitioner No.2 made enquiry on 21.6.83 and came to know on 22.6.83 on receipt of information from the Court that the plaintiffs obtained an ex parte decree on 16.1.83 in Title Suit No. 167/82 and thereafter on further enquiry came to know on 10.7.83 that they obtained an ex parte decree on 28.8.82 in Title Suit No. 706/81 and thereafter they filed the Miscellaneous Case on 14.7.83.

4. The plaintiffs contested the said Miscellaneous Case denying the material allegations and stating, inter alia, that the summons of the suit were duly served upon the defendants and there was no fraud or suppression of the said summons upon them. The defendant-petitioner opposite parties herein did not contest the said suit as they had no right, title and interest in the suit property in spite of the knowledge of the suit. Defendant opposite party No. 2 was found moving in the Court premises on the date of hearing of the suit.

5. Thereafter, trial of the Miscellaneous Case started on 16.7.86 when PW 1 Charu Chandra Chowdhury was examined and cross-examined and the case was fixed in 14.8.86 for further hearing. Thereafter on 14.8.86 the hearing of the case was adjourned to 25.9.86 on the application of the plaintiffs. Then on 25.9.86 PW 2 was examined on behalf of the defendant opposite parties herein and DW 1 was examined on behalf of the plaintiff- petitioners herein and the case was adjourned to 19.11.86 for further evidence on the prayer of plaintiff-petitioners herein. But on 19.11.86 plaintiff-petitioners herein did not adduce any further evidence and prayed for time but the Court below after rejecting prayer for adjournment by the impugned judgment allowed the Miscellaneous Case.

6. Mr. AY Salehuzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submitted that the Court below acted illegally in not considering the evidence of the DW 1 and the service return of the summons. He further submitted that plaintiff No. 2 Ali Azam, who was opposite party No. 2 in the said Miscellaneous Case, died on 20.8.86 and as his heirs were not substituted before passing the impugned judgment the case abated and, as such, the impugned order suffers from illegality.

7. Mr. S S Halder, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party, submitted that trial Court as the Court of fact having come to a definite finding that the service of summons was not satisfactory this Court in revision should not interfere with the said finding. He further submitted that the allegation of death of plaintiff No. 2 Ali Azam on 20.8.86 is not supported by any evidence and the supplementary affidavit filed on 8.9.93 is a fraudulent device of the petitioners and his client denied the allegations made in the said supplementary affidavit by filing an affidavit-in- opposition today.

<u>8. It appears from the impugned order that the Court below considered Ext. Ka(2), the return dated 11.1.82 of the service of summons of defendant Nos. 1, 4-8 and came to the conclusion that the service was not satisfactory, It appears from the said return that defendant No. 1 received the summons by signing his name and defendant Nos. 4, 5 and 7 were not present at their residence and the process-server tendered the summons on defendant No.8 for him and for defendant Nos. 4, 5 and 7 and he having refused to accept the same the process server served their summons with copy of plaint by hanging on 11.1.82. But there is no verified declaration of the process server under Order 5 rule 17 of the Code. There is no explanation about non-service of summons on defendant No. 6. Thereafter the Nazir made an endorsement on 16.1.82 of due service of summons upon the said defendant Nos. 1, 5, 7 and 8. It appears from the Order No.2 dated 3.2.82 that summons of the suit was served on the defendants and Court fixed the same for ex parte hearing on 14.3.82 as none of the defendants entered appearance overlooking that no summons was served on defendant No.6 and summons on defendant Nos. 4, 5, 7 and 8 was served by hanging under rule 17 of Order 5 of the Code. It was, therefore incumbent on the Court below to make an enquiry under rule 19 of Order 5 of the Code and record a distinct declaration of due service, if satisfied, or to order service afresh. This view finds support from the case of Mst. Johara Begum vs. Rafiqul Kader reported in 25 DLR 91. But the Court below without doing so fixed the suit for ex parte hearing. Defendant No.8 deposing as PW 1 denied that the process-server even tendered summons to him or he refused to accept the same whereas the process server deposing as DW 1 supported the said return of the service of summons. It appears from the impugned order that the Court below after considering the oral evidence of the PWs as well as DW 1 allowed the Miscellaneous Case on the view that the service of summons was not satisfactory and the opposite parties should get a chance to contest the suit. We have already noticed that no summons was served upon the defendant No. 6 and as such the suit could not be taken up for ex parte disposal on 28.8.82. Moreover, the Court below as the Court of fact has jurisdictiontorely on the evidence of PWs and not to rely on the evidence of DW 1 regarding service of summons. It is true in doing so Court below did not discuss the evidence of the said witnesses and assign reason for the same. But the fact remains that the Court which passed the impugned order recorded evidence of the said witnesses and heard the said witnesses deposing and also noticed their demeanours. In that view of the matter we find no fault in the Court below for not discussing the evidence of the witnesses in passing the impugned order. Court below, having found service of summons not satisfactory, gave the defendant-opposite parties herein a chance to contest the suit and, as such, we find no illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in setting aside the said ex parte decree.</u>

<u>9. Now coming to the objection raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the plaintiff No. 2 who was opposite party No. 2 in the said Miscellaneous Case died on 20.8.86 and, as such, the impugned order passed without substituting his heirs was illegal. From the application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed in this Court it appears that the said Ali Alam was shown as dead and his heirs joined as petitioner Nos. 2(a) to 2(1) in his place. But nowhere in the said application it has been stated that the said Ali Azam died on 20.8.86 during pendeney of the Miscellaneous Case before the Court below. Thereafter, the petitioners filed three applications, two under Order 5, rule 20 and one for substitution of the successor-in-office of the deceased opposite party No.1 Charu Chandra Chowdhury. But in none or these applications the date of death of the said Ali Azam was mentioned. But the petitioners filed a supplementary affidavit only on 6.9.93 alleging that the said Ali Azam died on 20.8.86 without being supported by any death certificate. Moreover, the trial of the Miscellaneous Case started on 16.7.86 and the learned Advocate of the plaintiffs in the Court below did not surrender his powers after 20.8.86 on the ground that one of his clients Ali Azam died on 20.8.86. On the other hand, the opposite parties in their affidavit-in-opposition dated 28.2.94 (sic) denied that the said Ali Azam died on 20.8.86 and asserted that there is no record of death of the said Ali Azam in the Thana District Sanitary Office or in the office of the Parishankhan Officer and as such there is no basis of his death on 20.8.86 as alleged and the supplementary affidavit has been filed only to create confusion without any basis for the allegation. We, therefore, find that the petitioners failed to satisfy us as to the alleged date of death of the said Ali Azam before passing of the impugned order. Moreover learned Advocate for the petitioners could not satisfy us that a Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure abates for non-substitution of the heirs of the deceased plaintiff-opposite party of such a case. So we find no merit in this contention also.</u>

10. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

Let the lower Court records be sent down along with a copy of this judgment expeditiously.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 738 of 2004
lawyer:
Dr Kamal Hossain, Senior Advocate, (Salauddin Ahmed & Sayeed Shahid Hussain, Advocates with him) instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
Rafique-ul-Huq, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mvi Md Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent 
Not represented ------ Respondent No.2.
parties:
Oriental Bank Ltd ------ Petitioner
Vs. 
Rina Alam and another  ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 12th April 2004 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 96 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J : The defendant No. 1- petitioner seeks leave to appeal against the judgment and decree dated 12-4-2004 passed by the High Court Division in Appeal from Original Decree No. 96 of 2002 affirming those dated 26-11-2001 of the Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 197 of 2001 decreeing the suit.

2. The respondent No.1 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 208 of 1997 renumbered as Title Suit No. 197 of 2001 against the petitioner bank for a declaration that the plaintiff had no liability to the petitioner bank for any loan amount, the so-called Memorandum of Deposit of Title Deed dated 17-3- 1988 was forged, concocted and illegal, the plaintiff is entitled to get back the title deed along with other supporting documents lying with the bank and a decree of Taka 75,00,000 as compensation against the petitioner bank.

3. The plaintiff filed the suit stating, inter alia, that her properties were mortgaged to the petitioner Bank in 1987 in connection with two loan liabilities of Gold Star Lines Ltd and Transbangla Shipping Company of one Shawkat Ali. On 17-11- 1988 both the loans were adjusted. Meanwhile, a loan in the name of Pan Asia Lines was sought for by her brother-in-law (Bhasur) Mr AB Siddiq but the said loan was not materialised. The plaintiff- respondent then sought return of the title deeds by letter dated 17-12-1992 but to no effect. In 1992 the bank filed Title Suit No. 147 of 1992 in Artha Rin Adalat claiming mortgage of the properties of the plaintiff-respondent on the basis of execution of Memorandum of Deposit of Title Deed and the Agreement to create further charge dated 17-3-1988. and 9-3-1989 respectively. The two documents were forged.

4. The defendant-petitioner bank filed written statement stating, inter alia, that on 29-2-1988 one AB Siddiq Ludu applied for Bai-Muajjal facility to the bank for purchase of two ships and also for adjustment of the loan of Taka 99,50,000 and offered to mortgage the property of the plaintiff which was given in mortgage against the loans of Shawkat Ali. Defendant bank sanctioned Bai- Muajjal facility and, in terms of the facility, the plaintiff on 17-3-1988 executed a memorandum of deposit of title deeds and deposited the original lease deed dated 28-10-1968 and original deed of sale dated 22-2- 1973 in the bank. On 17-3-1988, AB Siddiq Ludu also executed other charge documents. Thereafter, the plaintiff executed the agreement to create further charge on 9-3-1989. The Coast Marine Line Ltd have failed to adjust the loan of Taka 1,33,70,592 whereupon the bank instituted Title Suit No. 147 of 1992 renumbered as Title Suit No. 113 of 2000 in the 4th Court of Artha Rin Adalat for foreclosure and sale of mortgage and hypothecated properties including the property of respondent. By amendment of the written statement, the defendant bank further stated that they already obtained a decree from the Artha Rin Adalat on 24- 5-2001 and Artha Rin Adalat found the property of the plaintiff was mortgaged to the defendant bank. The present suit was therefore hit by the principle of res judicata.

5. The trial Court on the pleading framed the following issues for determination:

1. Was the suit in the present form maintainable?

2.	Was the suit bad for defect of parties?

3.	Had the plaintiff mortgaged the property covered by schedule deed against the loan of 	Coast Marine Line Ltd?

4. Was the suit barred by principle of res judicata?

5. What relief the plaintiff was entitled to?

6. The suit was decreed in part without any order as to costs declaring that the loan in respect of Messrs Gold Star Lines and Transbangla Shipping Company has been liquidated and the property in mortgage on that account being the subject-matter of title deed No. 788 dated 8-9-1972 is ordered to be returned to the plaintiff by the defendant No.1 Bank and that the memorandum of deposit of the alleged title deed dated 17-3-1988 is forged, colorable, illegal, fraudulent and inoperative.

7. An appeal therefrom at the instance of the defendant No.1 petitioner was, however, dismissed and forming the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court and the bank was directed to return the schedule documents within seven days of the receipt of the judgment.

8. Dr Kamal Hossain, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, has submitted that the matter in issue in the present suit being directly and substantial in issue in the Artha Rin Suit No.147 of 1992, the subsequent instant suit being Title Suit No.197 of 2001 being barred by principle of res judicata, the Courts below erred in law in holding that the decision of the Artha Rin Adalat could not operate as a bar of the present instant suit on the principle of res judicata. The learned Counsel has further submitted that the property in question having already been mortgaged with the bank against the liability of Transbangla Shipping Co and Gold Star Lines Ltd and that the same having also been mortgaged in respect of the loan of Messrs Coast Marine Lines Limited and that the petitioner having produced all relevant documents of mortgage including memorandum of deposit of title deeds, deed of agreement to create further charge duly signed by the respondent No.1, the original title documents, the written statement of respondent filed in 1995 in the bank suit making no claim therein for return of the title deed, the Courts below erred in law in holding that the petitioner bank has failed to prove the case of mortgage or execution of Exhibit E memorandum of deposit of title deed and deed of agreement to create further charge inasmuch as the plaintiff as DW 2 in the Artha Rin Adalat Suit No.147 of 1992 has admitted that she has mortgaged her Gulshan house with the AI-Baraka Bank as a security of loan against Messrs Gold Star Line and Messrs Transbangla Shipping Co owned by her brother-in-Iaw's son Md Shawkat Ali.

9. Mr Rafique-ul-Huq, the learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiff-respondent No.1, has, however, submitted that the Artha Rin Adalat Suit No. 147 of 1992/133 of 2000 being a suit for realisation of the loan amount in which the plaintiffs property has been illegally shown to be the collateral security for the loan due to Coast Marine Lines Ltd and that during the pendency of the said suit the plaintiff-respondent having filed the instant suit being Title Suit No. 208 of 1997/147 of 200 I for a declaration, inter alia, that the plaintiffs property alleged to have been mortgaged for the loan in respect of Coast Marine Lines Ltd. is forged, fraudulent, not binding upon the plaintiff did not come within the purview of section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the issue involved in the instant suit is not directly and substantially in issue in a former suit pending in the Artha Rin Adalat between the parties and no litigating under the same title by a competent civil Court treating subsequent suit is not res judicata inasmuch as not only the issue and the subject-matter are different but the Court is also not the same and of the same jurisdiction. The learned Counsel has further submitted that though Artha Rin Adalat Suit No. 147 of 1992/113 of 2000 was decreed on contest on 24-5-2001 wherein respondent No.1 's property was shown to be a collateral security, but upon an application dated 28-8-2001 by the respondent No.1 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure deleting the suit property thereby the decree was amended on 22-5-2002 deleting the property of respondent No.1 as security for the loan subject-matter of the decree against which order the petitioner bank has filed Writ Petition No. 3182 of 2002 which is pending.

10. Admittedly, Artha Rin Adalat Suit No.147 of 1992/13 of 2000 was filed for a money decree in respect of the loan amount allowed to Coast Marine Lines Ltd for a money decree of Taka 1,33,70,592 with interest and for realisation of the money by sale of mortgage property and the property described to the schedule in the plaint wherein respondent No.1's property was Included and it was stated in the plaint that the present plaintiff on 17-3-1988 created an equitable mortgage by depositing of title deed of her property mentioned in the schedule surety. The defendant in the said suit including the plaintiff- respondent No. 1 denying the claim of alleged mortgage, it may be mentioned here that the bank also did not claim that on 17-3-1988 the mortgagor executed a memorandum of deposit of title deed on 9-3-1989 and executed another agreement for creating further charge on the deed for the loan of Coast Marine Lines Limited. Admittedly, no issue on the basis of the said denial of the parties was framed regarding the disputed nature of mortgage as alleged in the said Artha Rin Adalat Suit. DW 1 Mr Azfar Ahmed, an officer of the Bank and tadbirkar, has deposed in that suit that the plaintiff- respondent No.1 was not a surety and that defendant No.4 did not keep the land in question as security for the loan but the instant case was a suit for the declaration, inter alia, that the plaintiffs property was not subject-matter of security in respect of the loan, the subject-matter of Artha Rin Adalat Suit No.147 of 1992.

11. Dr Kamal Hossain has referred to a decision in the case reported in AIR 1965 SC if 53 wherein it has been held that the provisions of section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure are not exhaustive with respect to the earlier decision operating as res judicata between the same parties on the same matter in controversy in a subsequent regular suit and on the general principle of res judicata, any previous decision on a matter in controversy, decided after full contest or affording fair opportunity to the parties to prove their case by a competent Court to decide, it will operate as res judicata in a subsequent regular suit. It is not necessary that the Court deciding the matter formerly be competent to decide the subsequent suit or that the former proceeding and the subsequent suit shall have the same subject-matter. The nature of the former proceeding is immaterial.

12. We do not dispute the proposition of law propounded in the said decision, rather the same has a persuasive force on us but in the facts and circumstances of the case the matter in issue was not at all in controversy in the previous suit and that the same was not litigated upon or any decision arrived at by the Artha Rin Adalat and, as such, the issue that has been decided on evidence in the instant suit could not operate as res judicata as no such issue was framed as to whether the property was the subject-matter of mortgage arrived at or decided in the previous Artha Rin Adalat suit and even the same is not litigated upon in the previous suit.

13. Dr Kamal Hossain also referred to the decision in the case of Manager, Bangladesh Krishi Bank and others vs Al-haj Md Nurul Islam and another reported in 52 DLR 434. The High Court Division held on the fact in that case that the question whether the plaintiff company suffered any loss or not due to laches, non-co-operation or activities of the Bank was considered and rejected in the earlier suit and that the suit was decreed against them and those adverse findings of the earlier suit do necessarily form the basis of res judicata in the subsequent suit.

<u>14. But in the instant suit as we have found that no such issue was framed regarding the subject-matter of present suit and decision was arrived at and the issue of the present suit was not directly or substantially an issue in the previous suit so as to render the present suit barred by the principle of res judicata. The High Court Division was not also unmindful as to the question of res judicata to operate as a bar in the instant suit and the trial Court as well on consideration of the material on record arrived at a finding that the suit is not barred by res judicata.</u>

15. The High Court Division on merit, on consideration of the evidence on record, arrived at a finding that:

"In the facts and circumstances of the case, such wild suggestion is not at all accepted. It is on record that after adjustment of the loans of Messrs Gold Star Lines and Trans Bangla Shipping Lines, another project of Pan Asia Lines for purchase of two vessels from London was submitted by Sirajul Alam and others and property of the plaintiff was offered as collateral. As project did not materialise, the plaintiff demanded return of her title deeds by letter dated 17-12-1992 which the bank received by putting the found seal of the bank. The bank did never deny the seal. Nor any step was taken to prove the seal forged.

The plaintiff deposited her original deeds in trust with the bank. The bank was required to take utmost care in dealing with such security, particularly in making further charge on the deeds. Admittedly, the bank never approached the plaintiff nor obtained any consent, oral or written, of the plaintiff for making further charge on the document. Such conduct is not becoming with the banking ethics, customs and practice. What disturbed us most is, how a bank could have created, without any consent of the plaintiff, further security on the deed already deposited in the bank in connection with and continuance of another loan.

In the circumstances, we find no reason to differ with the views of the learned Joint District Judge that the plaintiff did not execute the memorandum of deposit of title deed dated 17-3-1988 Exhibit E or the agreement for further charge dated 9-3-1989 Exhibit Land that she did not further mortgage her property to secure the loan of Messrs Coast Marine Lines Ltd."

16. The findings on merit arrived at by the High Court Division are concurrent finding of fact arrived at on consideration of the evidence on record. We have perused the same and could not persuade ourselves to disturb the same concurrently arrived at by the Courts below.

17. For the reasons as aforesaid, we find no substance in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioner to interfere with the impugned judgment of tile High Court Division.

This petition is accordingly dismissed.

End.

lawyer:
Garib Newaz, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner 
Kazi Md Shafiqul Hasan for Shafiq Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Jiban Bima Corporation Represented by its MD ------ Petitioner
vs
Md Mohibul Majid and another ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the order dated 10-8-89 passed by the Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No 2 of 1987 rejecting the petitioner's prayer for execution of the decree for permanent injunction under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit in the 1st Court of Munsif at Dhaka, being Title Suit No 122 of 1976, which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No 432 of 1982, for permanent injunction restraining the defendants opposite parties permanently from interfering with the plaintiffs possession in the property.

3. The suit was eventually decreed on contest and the said decree has been affirmed by the Superior Courts including the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. Thereafter the petitioner filed Title Execution Case No 2 of 1987 in the 4th Court of the Assistant Judge, Dhaka for execution of the decree, alleging inter alia that the decree of permanent injunction having been passed against the defendants, and it being binding upon them they were willfully disobeying injunction for which they are liable for action under Order 21 rule 32 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

4. The defendant-opposite parties filed written objection against the aforesaid application under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure contending inter alia that they have been in continuous possession in the suit property since before and as such there is no question of disobedience of the decree. It was also contended that the plaintiff petitioner has already filed an independent suit for recovery of khas possession in the suit property and as such the decree for permanent injunction has lost all it relevance and it cannot be executed.

5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge by his Order dated 10-8-89 dismissed the petitioner's application under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure holding inter alia that since the plaintiff petitioner has already started an independent suit, being Title Suit No 238 of 1984 in respect of the suit property admitting that the petitioner is not in possession of the suit property, the allegation, of violation of the decree does not stand. The learned Assistant Judge further found that since the petitioner has not adduced any evidence for proving willful violation of the decree of permanent injunction, the petitioner was not entitled to any relief in the case.

6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned order, the petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr Garib Newaj, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the learned Assistant Judge seriously erred in law in dismissing the petitioner's execution case on the erroneous view that since the plaintiff petitioner has already filed an independent suit for recovery of khas possession in the suit property the question of willful disobedience or violation does not arise and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that since there is no provision for adducing any evidence in execution proceedings under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in rejecting the petitioner's application on the ground that the petitioner did not adduce any evidence in support of his claim of disobedience and the same has occasioned failure of justice.

8. Mr Kazi Md Shafiqul Hassan, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, supports the impugned order and submits. that the learned Assistant Judge committed no error of law in passing the impugned order and it has not occasioned failure of justice to justify interference by this court exercising revisional power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

9. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has placed before me the impugned order as well as the application under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention Mr. Garib Newaj referred to me the case of Safar Ali Miah and others vs Badsha @ Siddique and others reported in 45 DLR 483. In this case a Division Bench of this Court with reference to sufficient cause on the subject held that for willful disobedience or violation of a decree for permanent injunction action under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure lies. In the case of Sashi Mohan Sen vs Ainullah, reported in 1992 BLD (AD) 8, the Appellate Division held that in a suit for permanent injunction when the judgment-debtor has the opportunity of, obeying the decree and he willfully failed to obey it, the decree may be enforced by detaining him in Civil prison or by the attachment of his property or by both.

10. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, it must be held that the learned Senior Assistant Judge clearly erred in law in dismissing the petitioner's application on the ground that the petitioner has already filed an independent suit for recovery of khas possession in the suit property and as such section under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is not available to the petitioner.

11. On the question of directing an enquiry as to where there has been a willful disobedience or violation of an order of injunction, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that there is no provision in the Code of Civil Procedure for taking evidence for ascertaining disobedience and consequently the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in asking for evidence. The learned Advocate further submits that in view of the admission by the opposite parties in their written objection, continued willful disobedience is an established fact and as such the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order on the ground of want of proof of willful disobedience and the same has occasioned failure of justice.

12. It is true, I do not find any provision in Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure or in the CROs for directing an enquiry on the truth or otherwise of the allegations of willful disobedience of violation of a decree for permanent injunction but the question is how a Court can take action against the alleged delinquent without any proof of the alleged violation without directing an enquiry into the matter to satisfy itself about the allegation against the defaulting judgment-debtor. With reference to section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure Mr Garib Newaj submits that procedures applicable to suit also apply to miscellaneous proceeding and, as such, there is no provision for taking evidence for ascertaining the truth of the allegation of willful disobedience of injunction in a miscellaneous execution proceeding and as consequently the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in rejecting the execution case on the ground of want of evidence. In support of his contention Mr Garib Newaj has referred to me the case of Manindra Nath Parial vs Saber Ahmed and others, reported in 1967 PLD (Dhaka) 621 wherein it has been held that section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not apply to execution proceeding. From this the learned Advocate for the petitioner argues that there is no scope for the Executing Court to embark upon an enquiry for ascertaining the truth or otherwise of the allegations of willful violation of the decree of permanent injunction. If this argument is accepted, it will mean that the Court shall have to act mechanically and blindly even on the unfounded allegation of or disobedience of an order of violation of an injunction and to punish the judgment debtor without affording him any opportunity of being heard. Such a situation is inconceivable on the simple reason that a Court of law cannot punish anybody without being satisfied on the basis of materials before him, that the judgment-debtor has willfully disobeyed or violated injunction. Such a course is also grossly violative of the principle of natural justice. Prudence, equity and good conscience revolt against such a preposterous proposition.

13. In view of the fact that 8 decree for permanent injunction remains in force forever the question of execution of the decree arises only when injunction is violated by the judgment debtor. Thus whenever the decree of permanent injunction is violated or willfully disobeyed the decree-holder becomes entitled to execution of the decree in accordance with the provision of Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure but before taking action under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against the delinquent the Court must be satisfied on evidence that the judgment-debtor has willfully disobeyed or violated injunction in defiance of the majesty of law. An enquiry on the truth or otherwise of the allegation of willful disobedience or violation of injunction by the judgment debtor is, therefore, essential before taking any punitive action against the delinquent.

<u>14. On consideration of the provision under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, it is evident that the decree for permanent injunction is executable and consequently the learned Assistant Judge clearly erred in law in dismissing the execution case on the ground that since the decree-holder has already filed an independent suit for recovery of khas possession, no action under Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is maintainable.</u>

15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any Order as to cost and the impugned order dated 10-8-89 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 2 of 1987 is set aside and the case is sent back on remand to the learned trial Court for a fresh hearing of the case after directing an enquiry as to whether there has been a willful disobeyance or violation of the decree of permanent injunction by the judgment debtors and to dispose of the execution case in accordance with law.

The learned Assistant Judge, Dhaka is directed to dispose of the execution case within 3 months from the date of receipt of the order.

Communicate the order to the leaned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka at once.

End.
